review_text: I have had several health watches and bands - Mifit series, Amazfit, E500, ED500, Polar, Fitbit that form the basis of this rating. I have had this watch for 9 days so this is an early review, and I will comment on setup, build, basic functions, heart rate, steps, bluetooth calling, exercise features, sleep tracking, app and general functionality: Setup: Instructions to get going were clear, app download and linking were seamless Build: this is an attractive watch with a beautiful high resolution and bright screen, and 4 buttons. So far I have used the screens it came with, but others are available for download. One of those included suited me just fine. Over the 9 days the battery life has gone from 100% to 30% so the prospects of getting 12 days or so battery life (AOD is not on) seem very good. Basic functions: Are as advertised and all seem to work. I have noticed that if I am out of range of the phone most of the time the bluetooth disconnects, and one has to relaunch the phone app to make it work. Bluetooth calling and linkage to the phone contacts work flawlessly. Exercise automatic detection kicks in after 4 or 5 minutes into the exercise, so it may be better to choose it to begin with. GPS turns on for outdoor walking etc Heart rate: does not match the polar heart rate strap or the Amazfit worn at the same time. Interestingly it behaves as the Amazfit used to before they upgraded the software - the timing of the fluctuations matches the exercise level, but the reported high readings are inflated relative to the Polar. Resting heart rate is very accurate. Steps: Match the other devices very very well Exercises - a lot of them are bundled, and I have tried only a few. They seem to work as expected and generate a record on the watch and the app Sleep tracking seems to match the other devices I have App: The app is clear and works well. However, there are features that could be improved. Data export and linkage to google fit or other apps for later processing - may only be of interest to techie. Most important is to solve autobluetooth reconnect. Blood pressure: I dont think the numbers produced are real, but there is a nice plotting utility for them. On my other watches they allow the user to enter the BP from a regular testing machine - taken at the same time as the watch reading. After doing this 2 or 3 times, the watch seems to calibrate and subsequent readings are accurate. This watch does not have that option, and would be good for them to add.
